key: Ask where the failure sits: hypothalamic and pituitary causes lower FSH and estradiol, ovarian causes raise FSH because feedback is lost, and outflow causes leave every hormone normal while blood cannot be built or escape.
items: GnRH neurons failed to migrate from the olfactory placode, so GnRH and smell are both missing.
Weight loss in a distance runner
Low energy availability slows GnRH pulses, the pattern of functional hypothalamic amenorrhea.
Severe undernutrition lowers leptin and GnRH pulse frequency, so FSH, LH and estradiol all fall.
Stress raises CRH and cortisol, which suppress hypothalamic GnRH release.
A lactotroph adenoma secretes prolactin, which suppresses GnRH and causes galactorrhea with amenorrhea.
Hypotension infarcts the enlarged pituitary of pregnancy, so lactation fails and gonadotropins fall.
A sella filled with CSF flattens the pituitary, which can lower gonadotropins or mildly raise prolactin.
Blocking D2 receptors removes the brake on lactotrophs, so prolactin rises and suppresses GnRH.
Oocytes are lost early and the ovaries become streaks, so FSH is high and estrogen is low.
FMR1 premutations cause early follicle depletion, a genetic cause of primary ovarian insufficiency.
Antibodies destroy follicles, often alongside Addison disease or thyroiditis, raising FSH before age 40.
Cytotoxic drugs kill growing and resting follicles, causing ovarian failure with a high FSH.
Curettage removed the basalis, and intrauterine adhesions prevent any endometrium from building up.
Menstrual blood collects behind a closed membrane, causing cyclic pain with normal hormones.
The uterus and upper vagina never formed, although ovaries, breasts and hormones are normal.
A band of tissue blocks the vagina, trapping menstrual blood above it despite normal ovarian function.
